WHAT CHANGED. One test, in one file: /Users/timothystockstill/code/macos/4thWAIV/agent-guard/.claude/worktrees/kit-walkthrough-targets/ts/metalang/guardrails.test.ts. `git status --short` shows that one file M; `git diff --stat` shows 21 insertions and 16 deletions in a single hunk, all of it the test formerly named `rule 1 weighs all twenty-four literals of app.tsx and leaves nine to the three kinds` and its own comment. Nothing committed. No rule code, no fixture, no other test, and no file outside this one is touched.

WHAT THE TEST NOW CHECKS. Renamed to `rule 1 leaves app.tsx these words, each to the kind that puts it outside the rule` (guardrails.test.ts:1365). It drops both totals — `languageWordsIn(app).length` was 24 and `wordsBySpelling(app).length` was 15 — because the test beside it, `writes no word of the language out`, already requires zero flagged across the whole drawing path. It drops `reported`, which prefixed each finding with `file:line`, and asserts `outsideTheRule(app).map(({ what }) => what).sort()`, so what is pinned is the word and the reason and nothing about position. The nine entries, read off the live file by running it, are one `"object" is a comparison against a JavaScript type`, six `"pending" is a member of this page’s own union of finding kinds`, and `"properties"` and `"property"` each `is English prose shown to the reader`. One entry per literal rather than one per distinct word, so a tenth exemption fails it; the reason carried in every entry, so one of the nine changing kind fails it; sorted, so moving or editing anything in app.tsx does not.

WHY SORTED. The fix note requires that editing anything above the exemptions not fail the test. Dropping the line number does that for a shift; sorting does it for a reorder as well, and costs nothing — a tenth exemption and a changed kind both still fail. This is a how, not a what: the assertion's content is exactly the nine word-and-reason pairs the note names.

THE OLD TEST'S COMMENT. It quoted the contract's counts ("the rule flags twenty-four literals in `app.tsx`; fifteen are the defect and nine are these three kinds") as the justification for asserting them. It is replaced by the sentence from contract decision `impact-test` that authorized this round, plus why each of the three things was dropped. The section header above the describe is NOT touched: it says the contract records fifteen literals as what IMPLEMENT clears, which is still a true statement about the contract.
